publicationRule: Only opportunities verified for Toppenish High School students. Current official opportunities need a current deadline or an open/rolling application; recurring plan-ahead items need an official source, a prior-cycle deadline, and an explicit warning that the next date may change.

scholarships.name: Mollie Davis Scholarship
scholarships.award: Up to $10,000/year for a bachelor's degree or $4,500/year for an associate degree
scholarships.eligibility: U.S. citizens who reside in Yakima County and will pursue a first associate or bachelor's degree full time.
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish residents qualify because Toppenish is in Yakima County. This is the countywide Mollie Davis program—not Yakima Rotary's school-limited Academic or Vocational scholarships.

scholarships.name: YVC Vineyard & Winery Technology Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Yakima Valley College Vineyard & Winery Technology Program
scholarships.eligibility: New or returning part-time or full-time YVC students pursuing a degree or certificate in Vineyard Technology or Winery Technology.
scholarships.expectedWindow: Open now — applications are accepted every quarter.
scholarships.whyFit: A direct local option for Toppenish students entering YVC's vineyard or winery technology programs; the official page says awards are available every quarter.

scholarships.name: Live Your Dream Award
scholarships.award: Local awards vary; recipients can receive up to $16,000 across award levels
scholarships.eligibility: Women who provide the primary financial support for themselves and dependents, are enrolled in or accepted to an undergraduate or vocational program, and do not hold or pursue a graduate degree.
scholarships.expectedWindow: Open now — applications are accepted August 1–November 15.
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish students are not excluded, but this is only for a student who supports dependents. It should be shared privately with students who may fit.

scholarships.name: Horse Heaven Hills Wine Growers Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: Students with a 3.0+ GPA studying viticulture, enology, wine business, or wine-related hospitality; preference goes to Yakima, Benton, or Klickitat County residents whose parent works in Washington's wine industry.
scholarships.expectedWindow: The 2026 application closed April 14; the 2027 date has not been released and may change.
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish is in Yakima County, one of the sponsor's preferred counties. The strongest match is a student with a parent employed in Washington's wine industry.

scholarships.name: Walter Clore Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: Students with a 3.0+ GPA studying a wine- or viticulture-related field at a Washington college, university, community college, or technical school.
scholarships.expectedWindow: The 2026 application closed April 14; the 2027 date has not been released and may change.
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish students can apply if their planned program is wine- or viticulture-related and they meet the sponsor's academic and enrollment rules.

scholarships.name: George & Susan Carter Scholarship
scholarships.award: $1,000 per year, renewable for up to four years
scholarships.eligibility: Students with a 3.4+ high school GPA pursuing viticulture, enology, or related food-science study; financial need is preferred.
scholarships.expectedWindow: The 2026 application closed April 14; the 2027 date has not been released and may change.
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish students are geographically eligible when pursuing an approved wine-related program and meeting the sponsor's GPA and enrollment rules.

scholarships.name: Dairy Strong Scholarship
scholarships.award: One $5,000 award and two $1,500 awards in the 2026 cycle
scholarships.eligibility: Washington dairy employees, immediate family of a dairy employee or owner, or students active in a dairy club or education program; any major and accredited university, trade school, or community college can qualify.
scholarships.expectedWindow: The 2026 application ran February 20–June 1; the 2027 date has not been released and may change.
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish students can qualify through their own or an immediate family member's work at a Washington dairy, or through an eligible dairy education program.

scholarships.name: Coca-Cola Scholars Program Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: Current Class of 2027 seniors who plan to attend an accredited U.S. college, have a 3.0+ GPA, and meet federal-aid citizenship/residency categories. Strong leadership and service record expected.
scholarships.expectedWindow: Open now; closes 5 p.m. Eastern / 2 p.m. Pacific
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish High School qualifies geographically because the program accepts students attending high school in any U.S. state. Individual applicants must also meet the listed citizenship/residency, 3.0 GPA, graduation-year, college-plan, and Coca-Cola family-employment rules.

scholarships.name: Washington State Opportunity Scholarship — Career & Technical
scholarships.eligibility: Washington residents within the income limit who will earn a high school credential by June, complete FAFSA or WASFA, and pursue an eligible associate degree, certificate, or apprenticeship. Applicants cannot already hold a bachelor's degree or plan to move directly into one after the funded program.
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish students qualify geographically as Washington residents; Yakima County also meets the Rural Jobs Initiative county rule. Each student still needs an eligible program and must meet income, financial-aid, and education-plan requirements.

scholarships.name: Elks Most Valuable Student Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: Current high school seniors who are U.S. citizens and will enroll full time in an accredited U.S. four-year undergraduate degree program. Permanent resident status alone does not qualify. No Elks family connection is required; judging considers academics, leadership, and financial need.
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish High School qualifies geographically because this is a national scholarship for U.S. high school seniors. Individual applicants must be U.S. citizens and plan a full-time four-year degree.

scholarships.name: BigFuture Scholarship: Start Your Scholarship List (Class of 2027)
scholarships.eligibility: U.S. residents in the Class of 2027 attending school in the U.S., a U.S. territory or possession, or a DoDEA school; must have a College Board account and plan to seek an associate or bachelor's degree. Save three scholarships to earn drawing entries. No essay, GPA, or test score required.
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish High School qualifies because the drawing accepts Class of 2027 students attending school in the U.S. Students must be U.S. residents and have a College Board account.

scholarships.name: QuestBridge National College Match
scholarships.award: Full four-year scholarships at participating partner colleges
scholarships.eligibility: High-achieving, low-income seniors currently attending high school in the U.S. and planning college the fall after graduation. QuestBridge has no absolute GPA or income cutoff, but finalists typically have very strong academics and substantial financial need.
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish High School qualifies because the National College Match accepts any senior currently attending high school in the U.S. Individual selection remains highly competitive and based on academics, finances, and personal qualities.

scholarships.name: Ewing C. Kelly Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: Washington high school seniors accepted to, or with an application pending at, an accredited college, community college, or technical college. U.S. citizenship or a green card is required; selection considers citizenship, achievement, activities, and financial need.
scholarships.expectedWindow: 2027 application is not released yet. The official 2026 application was postmarked by March 7; the next date may change.
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish High School qualifies because the official application accepts high school seniors throughout Washington. Individual students must also meet the citizenship/green-card and postsecondary-application requirements.

scholarships.name: Albert Lee Wright Jr. Memorial Migrant Scholarship
scholarships.organization: National Association of State Directors of Migrant Education
scholarships.eligibility: Graduating high school seniors eligible for Title I, Part C Migrant Education who plan postsecondary education. The program especially encourages students who have overcome barriers caused by moving for agricultural or fishing work.
scholarships.expectedWindow: 2027 application is not released yet. The official 2026 deadline was March 11; use that only as a planning estimate.
scholarships.whyFit: Toppenish High School is not excluded: this is a national program for all Title I, Part C-eligible graduating seniors. Only Toppenish students who are enrolled in Migrant Education and meet the program's mobility and financial-need requirements should apply.
